doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Her parents and the Three Cohens at Carnegie Hall
summary: Supportive parents of three jazz musicians; their mother waved at the Three Cohens sextet's Carnegie Hall show.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well you were mentioning your brothers. And I wonder how your parents have felt about three of their children in the world of jazz?

I don’t know they probably never thought they would retire. It was like what were you thinking? How did you let the three of us become jazz musicians? They, first of all the parents, I wish everybody had supportive parents like that, that see that their children,

they like something, they are into it and they are dedicated to it and they’re like okay we step out of the way, even if we have worries about how you’re going to survive and what’s going to happen, we’re going to let you do what you’re want to do and support you and help you pay for music lessons and drive you around and drive you around and drive you around, and go to all your youth orchestra concerts and, you know they were there when we were squeaking and they were there when The Three Cohens, with the three of us have a sextet and Avishai my younger brother the trumpet player, and Yuval, my older brother, the saxophone player, we have a sextet and when The Three Cohens Sextet played Carnegie Hall my mother was sitting in the audience and you know, and we introduced her and she got up and she was like doing the royal wave to everybody. So that’s the payment they get.
